question: A 58-year-old obese male has noticed the gradual development of a soft bulge on his right groin that has been present over the past year and occasionally becomes very tender. He notices that it comes out when he coughs and strains during bowel movements. He is able to push the bulge back in without issue. After examination, you realize that he has an inguinal hernia and recommend open repair with mesh placement. After surgery, the patient returns to clinic and complains of numbness and tingling in the upper part of the scrotum and base of the penis. What nerve was most likely injured during the procedure?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Open repair with mesh placement for inguinal hernia -> surgical manipulation near inguinal canal -> potential nerve injury -> 70% CHAIN: Numbness and tingling in upper part of scrotum and base of penis -> sensory nerve involvement -> likely ilioinguinal nerve injury -> 80% CHAIN: Ilioinguinal nerve injury -> sensory deficits in upper part of scrotum and base of penis -> consistent with patient's symptoms -> 70%
analysis: The patient likely has an injury to the ilioinguinal nerve, which is a branch of the first lumbar nerve. This nerve provides sensory innervation to the upper part of the scrotum and base of the penis. Injury to this nerve during inguinal hernia repair can result in numbness and tingling in these areas.
